hypothesis:
Third attempt, and the obstacle has changed. Attempt 2 compiled ENTIRELY FROM CACHE -- zero autotune lines in its log -- and trained 372 steps before a co-tenant arrived on gpu 5 and the guard aborted it at 17.5%% median MFU. So the concern that killed attempt 1, that a bf16 graph under max-autotune cannot compile inside the wall clock, is resolved: the warm cache from t0483 carries it. What remains is ordinary contention.

Second attempt at combining the two measured throughput gains. The first, t0483, timed out in evaluation; a re-serve of the identical source at t0490 was correctly rejected as a duplicate coordinate, which was my error -- I rebuilt the entry by stripping a compile revert and so reproduced a burned hash exactly. I had verified hashes for the exhaustive pair an hour earlier and did not repeat the check here.

Combine the two throughput gains nobody has combined. They are independent and both measured:
    lm_head bf16   +2.73% steps   (t0484, against the default-compile control)
    max-autotune   +2.26% steps   (t0445 control, against no autotune)
t0484 had to forfeit autotune to get a clean compile, which is exactly why it tied the champion at +0.000009 instead of beating it: it won -0.001188 against the control and handed back the same amount by dropping the search.

The cast's quality cost is negligible -- mechanism +0.000393, inside the 0.00085 floor -- so the precision worry about holding std-0.001 weights in an 8-bit mantissa did not materialise. That was the main risk and it is now measured rather than feared.

The obstacle is compile time: a dtype cast changes the traced graph, so t0483 missed the inductor cache, re-searched under max-autotune and exceeded the wall clock. But it compiled and trained 2729 steps before dying in evaluation, so the bf16 TRAINING graph is already cached. This is the t0432 -> t0433 pattern that produced a champion: the first attempt pays the search, the second reads it.

If both gains compose, steps should land near 2880-2890 against the champion's 2806, worth roughly -0.0016 -- which would be the largest promotion since t0433.
change_summary: self.lm_head.to(dtype=torch.bfloat16) beside the existing wte and value-embedding casts, with torch.compile left at the champion's max-autotune-no-cudagraphs. This is deliberately the configuration that timed out at t0483 -- the difference is that its training graph is now in the shared cache. The eval graph may still be cold, which is the specific way this can fail.
expected_val_bpb_effect:
Step count is the mechanism, as with every throughput bet. If the cache carries the compile, I expect ~2880 steps against the champion's 2806 (+2.7%), worth about -0.0016.
The registered failure mode is a third timeout. t0483 died in EVALUATION, and the eval path compiles its own graph -- which is precisely what defeated the depth-13 warm retries at t0438. If that happens here, the eval graph will then be cached too and a further attempt becomes cheap; if it happens twice more I stop, because at that point the cast and autotune are simply incompatible within this wall clock and t0484's standalone version is the honest ceiling.
risk:
Spending a slot on a configuration that has already timed out once, which I have done before and which worked twice (t0433, t0437) and failed twice (t0438, t0481). The difference between those cases was whether the EVAL graph got cached, not the training graph, and I do not know which side of that line this falls on.
If it wins, the champion would carry both a bf16 lm_head and max-autotune, and the second is already known to make every future structural bet expensive -- it is what forces the compile revert on graph-changing trials. Promoting this makes the campaign faster and further experiments harder, which is a real trade rather than a free win.
